newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom's Xtra site raises concerns - NZCC.
newsitem.headline: Telecom's Xtra site raises concerns - NZCC.

text.p: Monopolies watchdog, the New Zealand Commerce Commission, said on Wednesday Telecom Corp's internet service provider, Xtra, raised competition concerns.
The commission said it had received 15 complaints from other internet service providers (ISPs) that Telecom was breaching the Commerce Act.

The complaints say Telecom is supplying Xtra cheaper than that offered by suppliers, that Telecom is refusing competitors access to a new Internet service IPNet and that Telecom was deliberately running Xtra at a loss to drive competitors out of the market.
Commission chairman Alan Bollard said the commission was concerned that running Xtra at a very substantial loss may breach the Act. It was investigating.

"The commission must address the question, are Xtra's losses for the first few years a legitimate investment to gain a foothold in the rapidly exapnding Internet services market, or is such a strategy anti-competitive behaviour and prohibited by the Act," he said.
"The commission is concerned tha Xtra's alleged below cost pricing and the level of loss being incurred may be contrary to the Act," he said.
He said there was no evidence that Telecom was selling its 0800 services at cheaper rates that offered to other ISPs.

On the claims that Telecom was refusing competitors access to IPNet, the commission found that the IPNet was still being trialled and had not yet been commercially launched so there was unlikely to be a breach of the Act.
